title: A study of JNJ-78934804 in participants with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (DUET ENCORE-UC)
official: A phase 3 randomized, double-blind, and active controlled, multi-center study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of JNJ-78934804 in participants with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis
summary:
Background and study aims
Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic disease of the large intestine. Although targeted therapies have improved treatment for UC, many participants do not respond or eventually stop responding to a single therapy, especially after trying multiple treatments. Therefore, exploring new approaches such as combining advanced therapies may help improve outcomes.
JNJ-78934804 is a fixed-dose combination* of guselkumab and golimumab. Guselkumab binds to interleukin-23 (IL-23), and golimumab binds to tumour necrosis factor alpha (TNFα). IL-23 and TNFα normally cause inflammation. By blocking them, this medicine helps reduce the inflammation that occurs in UC.
* Single product containing two drugs in a fixed amount
** Specific types of proteins involved in inflammation
In this study, researchers want to assess how well JNJ-78934804 works compared with guselkumab in participants with UC at Week 48.

Who can participate?
Participants aged 18 years or older with moderately to severely active UC.

What does the study involve?
The study consists of:
1.	Screening period (up to 6 weeks)
2.	Double-blind treatment period (up to 48 weeks)
2.1. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the following groups:
2.1.1. JNJ-78934804 group: Participants will receive JNJ-78934804 induction doses administered under the skin at Weeks 0, 4 and 8, followed by maintenance doses every 4 weeks (q4w) from Week 12
2.1.2. Guselkumab group: Participants will receive guselkumab induction doses administered under the skin at Weeks 0, 4 and 8, followed by guselkumab maintenance doses every 4 weeks (q4w) from Week 12
2.2. Participants who meet rescue criteria will receive JNJ-78934804 induction doses at Weeks 16, 20 and 24, followed by JNJ-78934804 maintenance doses every 4 weeks (q4w) from Week 28
3.	Long-term extension period (up to 96 weeks)
All randomly assigned and treated participants will complete a safety follow-up visit approximately 12 weeks after their last dose of study intervention.
Safety assessments will include monitoring of adverse events, vital signs, electrocardiograms (tests that record heart activity), clinical laboratory assessments and pregnancy testing.
The overall duration of the study will be approximately 3 years.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
There is no established benefit to participants taking part in this study. Based on scientific theory, JNJ-78934804 may improve ulcerative colitis. However, this cannot be guaranteed because JNJ-78934804 is still being investigated and it is not known whether it will be effective.
In addition, participants assigned to the guselkumab treatment group may not receive JNJ-78934804 and may receive only guselkumab during the study, unless otherwise specified.
Participants may experience benefits unrelated to receiving the study drug, such as regular visits and assessments that monitor their overall health. Participation may also help improve treatment for people with UC in the future.
Participants may experience side effects from the study drugs or procedures. These may range from mild to severe and, in some cases, may be life-threatening. Potential risks include:
1.	Worsening of UC
2.	Serious infections and reactivation of latent infections
3.	Hypersensitivity (exaggerated immune response) reactions
4.	Malignancy (the presence of cancerous cells that grow in an uncontrolled manner)
5.	Congestive heart failure (a condition in which the heart is unable to pump blood efficiently)
6.	Demyelinating disorders (conditions that damage the protective myelin sheath surrounding nerve fibres)
7.	Lupus-like syndrome (a condition that may be triggered by prolonged use of certain medications, including TNFα inhibitors)
8.	Liver injury
9.	Haematologic reactions (immune or non-immune responses involving blood products)
Risks associated with study procedures include video endoscopy, which may result in bleeding or intestinal perforation (formation of a hole in the intestine).
There are also other, less frequent risks. The participant information sheet and informed consent form, which all participants must sign before taking part, contain detailed information about the known risks of participation.
Not all possible side effects and risks associated with JNJ-78934804 are currently known. During the study, the sponsor may obtain new information about JNJ-78934804. Participants will be informed as soon as possible of any new information that may affect their decision to continue participating, including any newly identified risks.
To minimise risk, participants will be monitored regularly for side effects and other medical events. Participants will be instructed to report any concerns to the study doctor, who will provide appropriate medical care. Any serious side effects reported to the sponsor will be thoroughly reviewed by a specialist drug safety team.
There is no cost to participants for taking part in the study. The sponsor will pay for the study drug and all study-related tests. Participants will receive reasonable reimbursement for study-related expenses, such as travel and parking costs.

Where is the study run from?
Janssen-Cilag International NV

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
August 2026 to October 2030

Who is funding the study?
Janssen Research & Development, LLC (USA)

conditions: Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Diagnosis of ulcerative colitis (UC) established at least 12 weeks before screening including both endoscopic evidence and a histopathology report consistent with a diagnosis of UC.
2. Moderately to severely active UC defined as baseline (Week 0) modified Mayo score of 5 to 9, inclusive, using the Mayo endoscopy subscore obtained during central review of the screening video endoscopy
3.  An endoscopy subscore >=2 as obtained during central review of the screening video endoscopy
4.  Have had an inadequate initial response, loss of response, or intolerance to previous approved systemic therapies
Exclusion criteria:
1. Isolated proctitis (UC limited to the rectum only or to less than [<] 20 centimeter [cm] from the anal verge) as determined during central review of the screening video endoscopy OR Has a diagnosis of isolated proctitis
2. Diagnosis of indeterminate colitis, microscopic colitis, ischemic colitis, Crohn’s colitis or any findings suggestive of CD
3. Has a history of or ongoing chronic or recurrent infectious disease 
4. Has previously demonstrated inadequate initial response, loss of response, allergy, hypersensitivity or intolerance to guselkumab or to golimumab
5. Is a participant who is pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant, or plans to father a child, while enrolled in this study or within 6 months after the last dose of study intervention
